title: Headaches — red-flag warning signs
content: Call 999 or go to A&E if a headache comes with a seizure (fit), numbness or weakness in the body or face, a sudden and extremely painful onset, a head injury within the last 3 months, difficulty speaking, keeping balance, walking, or remembering things, drowsiness or confusion, loss of vision, a rash that does not fade when a glass is rolled over it, or a very high temperature with a stiff neck and sensitivity to bright light. See a GP if you have tried treating a headache yourself and it is not improving or is getting worse, or if you regularly get headaches.
